# Roverlands world

A 1536 m square world generated from a seed, the same on every machine, plus the code that draws it.

* `worldgen.js` — the generator (pure: no DOM, no three.js, no Rapier). `generateWorld({ seed, vehicles, map })`; also `'moon'` and `'station'` (see "The Moon" / "Lantern Station" at the end);
  `map: 'classic'` (default — this 1536 m world, the Sandbox / Flag Run map) or `'county'` (Wayfare County, see
  "Wayfare County" at the end — generated by `county/`).
* `roads.js` — routing, smoothing, height profile and carving of the road network.
* `scatter.js` — where every tree, bush, reed bed, rock and log goes, and the ground decor.
* `wmath.js` — maths that agrees bit for bit across browsers (see "Same world everywhere").
* `world-async.js` + `world-worker.js` — `generateWorldAsync(opts, onProgress)`: the same generator in a module worker,
  the accessors rebuilt on the page (`attachWorldFns`); falls back to the direct call.
* `world-data.js` — every table: SURFACES, biomes, biome anchors, fixed places, road classes, object kinds, scatter rules.
* `../client/world-view/` — the renderer (`index.js` is the entry point; see "The view").
* `../../world.html` — a dev page to fly round a world: `world.html?seed=7&quality=medium&at=canyon`.

Tests: `node --test prototypes/roverlands/tests/world.test.js` (generator) and
`flock /home/radgh/claude/agent/roverlands-pw.lock npx playwright test prototypes/roverlands/tests/world.spec.js`
(the page; screenshots in `tests/shots/world-*.png`).

## The layout

x runs east, z runs south, the origin is the middle of the map. Home is on the **south** edge; everything you go to
is north of the river, so every Flag Run crosses it.

```
 z = -768  north   Saltwind Dunes        Whitecap Heights (summit flag)        Rustgate Canyon
                   (sand, ridges)        snow, frozen Rime Pond                mesas, terraces, the Mesa Crown
                                         Tallpine Ridge (pine, ridged hills)    flag on a mesa with a switchback
                   Brackwater Fen (mud, pools, fallen logs, reeds) — Fen Heart flag in the middle
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Wending River (west -> east, falling ~4.6 m) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
                   Shingle Ford (x -330)        Old Timber Bridge (x 80)          Otter Ford (x 330)
                   River Bluff flag on the north bank (x ~ -120)
                   Haystead Farms (fields, fences, bales)   Glassmere (lake)   Paleleaf Wood (birch)
 z = +768  south               Long Meadow  —  Home base (garage row, 16 pads)  —  Sandbox lot (8 pads)
```

Biomes come from ~40 anchor points (`ANCHORS`) jittered per seed and seen through a domain warp, so borders wander.
A sample belongs to its nearest anchor's biome; heights blend between the nearest few anchors over 75 m. Each seed
moves the anchors, the river's meanders and every noise field, but keeps this macro layout, so every map has the
same kinds of challenge.

### Biomes

| id | key | shows as | ground | height shape | what grows / stands there |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | meadow | Long Meadow | grass, dirt patches | rolling, 7-16 m | odd oaks, bushes, stones |
| 1 | pine | Pine ridge | grass + forest floor, rock on steep | ridged hills, 16-50 m | dense pine/spruce/fir, logs, boulders |
| 2 | birch | Birch wood | grass, dirt patches | rolling, 9-20 m | birch groves, saplings, bushes |
| 3 | bog | Mudflats | **mud** (soft, sink 0.12), grass hummocks, shallow pools | flat, ~2 m | **fallen logs**, reeds, dead snags, bramble |
| 4 | river | River valley | grass, gravel bars and mud at the water | floodplain + valley walls | willows, bushes, river stones |
| 5 | canyon | Red-rock canyon | dirt, rock on every riser | terraced mesas, 14-50 m; the flag mesa 72 m | rocks, boulders, juniper, kickers |
| 6 | dunes | Dunes | sand | crests across the wind, 8-21 m | a little scrub, kickers |
| 7 | snow | Snowy uplands | snow above ~44-54 m, rock on steep, **ice** pond | a dome peaking ~140 m | frost firs, rocks |
| 8 | farm | Farmland | **farm** soil in 70 x 46 m fields, grass margins | almost flat | **fence lines**, round hay bales, oaks |
| 9 | lot | Sandbox lot | dirt, gravel by the pads, a **mud pit** | flat, with a banked loop track | ramps, jumps, crates, barrels, bales |

### Water

* **The river** is a function of x (one centreline z per column), `PLACES.river` waves + noise, half-width 10-15 m,
  ~2.75 m deep in the middle. Steep banks (4.5 m) where it is deep; you must go round.
* **Two fords** (`PLACES.fords`): the channel widens 1.6x, the bed rises to 0.35-0.45 m under the water, the banks
  ease out over 14 m (about 12 %). Surface `shallows`. The road runs straight through, following the bank exactly
  (a ford road is never smoothed or carved — smoothing put a lip at the water's edge).
* **The bridge** (`PLACES.bridge`, x 80): a straight deck ~56 m, 6.4 m wide, 2.6 m above the higher bank, two rails,
  two stone piers. Objects `bridge_deck` / `bridge_rail` / `bridge_pier`; `sites.bridges[0]`.
* **Glassmere**: a 46 m lake bowl, ~3.4 m deep; the roads go round it. **Fen pools**: shallow (≤ 0.45 m) water in the
  hollows the fen-pool noise digs (only there — an earlier version flooded the low riverbank inside the fen).
* **Rime Pond**: frozen — surface `ice`, no water.
* `world.water` holds the water SURFACE height per sample (NaN = dry); `waterAt(x, z)` interpolates it and returns null
  where the ground is above it.

### Roads

`ROAD_CLASSES`: `road` (7.2 m wide, surface road, grade clamp 18 %), `gravel` (5.4 m, surface gravel, 19 %),
`track` (3.8 m, surface dirt, 34 % — the rough ways). The network (`EDGES` in worldgen.js):

* home → sandbox, both fords, the bridge; each crossing → the junction north of the river → Tallpine Ridge;
* ford W → **Fen Heart** (gravel causeway into the mud), junction → **River Bluff**, ridge → **Whitecap Summit**,
  ford E → canyon base → **the switchback** (gravel) → **Mesa Crown**;
* tracks: home → farm → ford W, fen → dunes → ridge, canyon → ridge, sandbox → ford E.

How a road is made (`roads.js`):

1. **Route** — A* on a 16 m grid. The search state is (cell, heading): a step may not turn more than ~100 degrees from
   the last, so a hairpin takes two steps and its legs end up a cell apart. On an 8 m grid with no heading, A* stacked
   hairpin legs closer than a road is wide and they carved over each other (steps of 2 m). Steps over the class's
   maxGrade are not allowed; deep water is a wall except in a ford; a cell another road already uses is cheaper, so
   roads join.
2. **Smooth** — Chaikin corner cutting, then a point every 2 m. Grid points that crowd the true end are cut (otherwise
   a path ran to the nearest grid cell past the flag and back).
3. **Profile** — the land's height along the road, box-filtered twice, eased into the pinned heights at both ends,
   kept above any water, then clamped to the class's grade with a forward and a backward pass. Where the road runs
   over an earlier road's surface it is pinned to it (and clamped again).
4. **Carve** — roads are carved one at a time in class order, each one read from the land as the earlier ones left it.
   Every sample within halfW of the road takes the profile height (plus up to 3 % banking on bends), the shoulder
   blends back into the land, and the driving surface of an earlier road is never re-carved.

**The switchback** up the Mesa Crown is drawn by hand (`switchbackTrack`): four 110 m legs 18 m apart joined by 9 m
half-circle hairpins, climbing from the canyon floor (20 m) to the top (72 m) at one steady ~9 % grade. The apron under
it takes the height of the nearest bit of track and is then smoothed between the benches, so the slope between legs
is a steep bank you cannot shortcut.

The test holds roads and gravel roads to ≤ 28 % over any 4 m on the finished ground (the clamp is 18-19 %; the rest is
banking and bilinear interpolation). On 12 seeds checked by hand, none went over 25 % after the fixes above.

### Sites

* `home` — the flag ring (r ≈ 14 m) on a 120 x 64 m paved pad; 16 pads in two rows facing north, four open sheds behind.
* `pads` — 16 at home + 8 in the sandbox; `vehicle` cycles through `opts.vehicles` (default `['trail_jeep','dirtbike']`).
* prop pads — after the 24 vehicle pads (the room numbers entities in pad order): crates, bags, barrels, jetpacks at
  home, two balls and four crates in the sandbox, a crate at every flag. `prop: true`.
* `runway` — 300 x 20 m, flat, paved, empty, in the meadow between Glassmere and home (`PLACES.runway`).
* `flags` — river, bog, canyon, summit, each > 400 m from home, each on a small flat spot at the end of its road.
* `ramps` — the sandbox set (small 4 m x 0.7 m, medium 6 x 1.5, big 9 x 2.8, two table-top jumps with landing ramps)
  plus six kickers out in the world (dunes, canyon, meadow), all `wedge` objects.
* `labels` — region, base, water, crossing and flag names for the map. Every name is original.

### Objects

`world.objects[i].id === i`. ~5.9k on seed 7 (`SCATTER.density` is the one knob): ~1.7k pines, 0.9k birches, 170 oaks,
450 saplings, 750 bushes, 210 reed beds, 220 logs, ~950 rocks and boulders, 500 fence panels, ~50 bales, crates,
barrels, signs, ramps, the bridge and sheds. ~13k decor items (ferns, flowers, mushrooms, pebbles, reed tufts, branch
piles) in `world.decor`, drawn only near the camera, never simulated.

| kind | collider (at s = 1) | breakAt (N·s) | fall |
|---|---|---|---|
| tree_birch | cyl r 0.15, h 6 | 9000 (r < 0.12) / 16000 / 26000 | topple |
| tree_pine | cyl r 0.26, h 7 | 16000 typical, null when r ≥ 0.3 | topple |
| tree_oak | cyl r 0.42, h 5 | null (26000 when s < 0.75) | topple |
| sapling | cyl r 0.06, h 1.8 | 3000 | topple |
| bush / reeds | cyl r 0.55 / 0.45 | 800 / 250 | flatten |
| fence | box 1.2 x 0.6 x 0.06 | 4000 | topple |
| log | box (round: 'z') r 0.35, 5-8 m long | null | — |
| rock_s/m/l, boulder | cyl r 0.45 / 0.95 / 1.8 / 2.8 | null | — |
| crate / barrel / hay_bale / sign | box 0.5 / cyl 0.36 / cyl 0.75 / cyl 0.1 | 2500 / 3000 / 6000 / 3500 | shatter / topple |
| ramp, bridge_*, shed | wedge / box | null | — |

Placement rules (scatter.js): dry ground (reeds may stand in ≤ 0.35 m of water), off every road by the kind's own
margin, not too steep for the kind, clear of the home pad, the sandbox, flags, bridge ends and ramps, and not crowding
anything already placed (4 m spatial hash). Logs also need both ends dry, off the road and within 1 m of the same height.

## Same world everywhere

Object ids are indices, so "object 812 broke" must mean the same tree on every player's machine. `+ - * /` and
`Math.sqrt` are correctly rounded everywhere; `Math.sin / cos / exp / pow / atan2 / hypot` are not, and a tree sitting
exactly on a threshold could exist in Chrome and not in Safari. So nothing that decides a height, surface or object
uses them: `wmath.js` has polynomial `dsin` / `dcos`, and the noise is highdef-3d's `noise.js` (integer hashes and
polynomials only). Yaw angles handed to the renderer may use atan2 (a 1e-16 rad difference changes nothing shared).
`worldHash(world)` hashes heights + surfaces + objects; the room can compare it.

## The view (`js/client/world-view/`)

| file | what it does | reuse |
|---|---|---|
| `index.js` | `createWorldView` — boot order, per-frame update, post chain, the contract API | imports highdef `sky.js`, `materials.js`, `postfx.js` |
| `quality.js` | low / medium / high presets | own numbers |
| `ground.js` | 128 m chunks, LOD steps 2/4/8/16 m (the finest IS the physics grid), skirts, 12 surfaces in one texture array, triplanar rock | copy-and-change of highdef `terrain.js` (it is welded to highdef's 5-surface biome table); textures painted by highdef `kit/textures.js` |
| `water.js` | river + lake + pools as one mesh with a per-vertex surface height, two-phase flow map downstream, depth colour, white water at the fords | copy-and-change of highdef `water.js` (that one is a single flat sea level) |
| `grass.js` | world-anchored blade lattice, mask from SURFACES + roads, hand-filtered height lookup (phones often cannot filter float textures), 4 push points | copy-and-change of highdef `grass.js` (it reads highdef's biome table) |
| `things.js` | every object + decor: near ring instanced per model, far cells baked; breaking, flattening, falling pieces | models from highdef `kit/trees.js` + `kit/rocks.js`, materials after highdef `vegetation.js` (copied because highdef lets a model pick its own random size; ours must match the collider) |
| `tracks.js` | tyre ruts: 4-point cross-section (raised light lips, dark pressed trough), depth from `SURFACES[].rut`, fade after 2 min, ring buffer | new |
| `particles.js` | dust in the surface's colour, water spray | new |
| `mapimage.js` | top-down map canvas: biome colours, surfaces, water, hill shade, roads (labels drawn by the HUD) | new |

Sizing: every model is scaled to its collider (tree height = kind h x s, rock footprint and height = its cylinder,
crate = its box), never a size the kit picked.

### Performance (seed 7, measured 2026-10-25)

* Generation: ~1.0-1.1 s in Node 22 and in headless Chromium on this VM (land 280 ms, roads 290, surfaces 215,
  planting 145, river 100). The game builds every world in a worker (`world-async.js`, see "Wayfare County"), so
  the load screen keeps moving on a phone.
* Draw calls on **medium** (1280 x 720, shadow passes included): 80-190 depending on where you look. Triangles
  0.5-0.8 M. Low (402 x 780): see the spec log line `low {...}`.

## How to add a biome

1. Add a row to `BIOMES` (append — the id is stored per sample) and anchors to `ANCHORS`.
2. Add its height function to the `H` array in worldgen.js (same index).
3. Give it a surface rule in the surfaces switch, scatter rules in `SCATTER.biomes` / `SCATTER.decor`, and a router
   cost in `biomeCost` if roads should avoid it.
4. Ground look: the vertex tint comes from `BIOMES[].tint`; if it needs a new texture, add a `LAYERS` row in ground.js
   and a `SURF_LAYER` entry.

## How to add an object kind

1. A row in `KINDS` (collider size at s = 1, breakAt, mass, fall, h if it is sized by height).
2. Place it: a scatter rule, or by hand in worldgen.js with `addObj` / `propAt`.
3. Draw it: a model in `buildModel` in things.js (kit builder or a `Builder` geometry carrying position, normal, uv,
   color, aWind), and if it is not sized by height, a branch in `matrixFor`.

## Wayfare County (map `'county'`, Expansion 1 M3)

`generateWorld({ seed, map: 'county' })` / `generateWorldSteps(...)` — the expansion's big map. Code in `county/`:
`countygen.js` (the generator), `cities.js` (a town's streets, buildings and landmark yards), `county-data.js` (every
place, name, town, style and scatter rule — change numbers there). Same contract and same purity rules as the classic
world (no Math.sin/cos/exp/pow/hypot in anything that decides a height, surface or object). The classic world is
untouched: `tests/county.test.js` pins its hash (seed 7 = `7ddb12eb`, seed 1234 = `2ef6b2b2`).

* **3072 m square, 2 m cell, dim 1537** (2.36 M samples; heights + water + roadDist are 9.4 MB each).
* **Generation**: ~3.3-3.8 s in Node 22 on this VM (seed 7), and **in a worker** in the page (`world-async.js`
  `generateWorldAsync()` -> `world-worker.js`; the accessors are rebuilt on the page from the transferred arrays;
  `?worker=0` or a failed worker builds on the page instead). `world.builtIn` says which. `world.stats.steps` has the
  split (ms, Node): masks ~250, land ~1450, scree ~45, plateau + river ~190, stamps ~150, roads ~380, water + surfaces
  ~480, objects ~380.
* **V8 and big functions**: V8 will not optimise a function with too much bytecode, and `generateCountySteps` is past
  that limit — everything in it ran 2-3x slower (7.7 s instead of 3.4 s) the moment it grew. Every hot loop in it is
  therefore its own closure (`(() => { for ... })()`), which V8 optimises on its own. Keep new per-sample loops in a
  closure (or a top-level function) too.
* **Slopes** (share of dry land): past 63 deg seed 7 ~2.3 %, seed 1234 ~2.6 % (before M3b: 2.24 % / 1.83 %; classic
  0.31 %); past 45 deg ~9 % (classic 1.9 %). Highest ground ~390 m (Thornhorn; classic 138 m).

### The layout

```
 z = -1536 north   Greyspine Mountains (Thornhorn, Wardenspire; snow > ~225 m)     Rustwild badlands (terraced mesas)
                   Elderwood (giant trees)   Highgate on its plateau (176 m, sheer 74 m rim, switchback up a spur to the south)
                   Brokenback Scarp: a 30 m cliff step across the vale (ramps at its gaps)
                   Lindell Water + Port Lindell       Vale Crossroads        Tollen Gorge (40-90 m sheer walls)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~ Tollen River, west -> east: through the lake, a ford, the gorge, out east ~~~~~~~~~~~~
                   Marrow Flats + farm belt (10 plots, Marrow Barn)        Copper Hills + Copperton
 z = +1536 south                    Wayfare Field (1.1 km runway)                          Skyreach Launch Site
```

* **Terrain**: a rolling base; ridged vale hills wherever nothing else is; the **mountains**; the **Copper Hills**
  (ridged, half-terraced); the **Rustwild** (terraced mesas: 15 m steps with sheer risers); the **plateau** (flat top, a 74 m cliff over 13 m, a talus skirt);
  the **scarp** (a cuesta: 30 m cliff, long gentle dip slope behind it); the **river** (a function of x like the
  classic river, so the water view works unchanged) with a flat **lake** stretch, a **ford** (Pebblerun Ford) and the
  **gorge** stretch where the bed narrows between sheer walls that climb until they meet the land.
* **Mountains, hills, mesas use GRADIENT noise** (`gnoise` / `ridgedG` / `gfbm` in countygen.js: twelve slope
  directions, each octave turned 36.87 degrees — the rotation (0.8, 0.6) is exact — and 2.03x finer; integer hashes and
  + - * only, so the same everywhere). wmath's value noise interpolates heights on a square lattice and its ridges ran
  along the lattice: from the air the range read as blocks. The mountains are 3 octaves with gain 0.36 (big smooth
  forms; a crest rounded over a few metres by a soft abs, which also keeps the share past 63 deg where it was), seen
  through a 150 m domain warp; 26 m strata cliff bands only where a slow mask says so. The vale hills come from a 4 m
  lattice of the same noise (the old 8 m lattice creased them along its rows).
* **Named peaks** (`C.peaks`): Thornhorn (~390 m) and Wardenspire (~350 m). Within `r` the range's own ridged noise is
  lifted toward the peak's height (no strata rings round a summit), so each is a massif whose ridges run up to a top.
  Each is a `sites.survey` summit and a map label.
* **Scree** (`C.scree`, step 2c): the land is box-blurred over 13 samples; wherever the blur is above the ground (the
  concave foot of a cliff) the ground rises part of the way to it (mountains 0.7, hills 0.5, badlands 0.42). Only
  concave ground moves, so crests and cliff tops stay sharp. Where it rose > 1 m the surface is gravel.
* **Biomes** appended to `BIOMES` (ids 10-21, `c_*`; `river` reuses id 4). Rows may carry `forest` (how much grass
  draws as forest floor) and `tintK` (tint strength) — ground.js reads both, classic rows leave them out.

### Roads (grade caps)

Classes appended to `ROAD_CLASSES` (the profile clamp is the cap; the finished ground reads up to ~0.04 more over a
4 m window because the carve stamps each cell with its nearest 2 m sample — the test allows for that):

| class | width | clamp (cap) | finished-ground limit in the test | used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `highway` | 9.2 m | 7 % | 10 % | town to town (Marrow Flats - Port Lindell - Crossroads - Copperton, Marrow Flats - Copperton) |
| `lane` | 7.2 m | 11 % | 16 % | the switchback (10 % legs, 5.5 % hairpins), airfield, launch site, east bridge, Rustwild Gate |
| `street` | 8.4 m | flat | 12 % | town grids |
| `mountain` (gravel) | 6 m | 12 % | 17 % | Highgate to Greyspine Lookout, Port Lindell to the Elderwood; the router's own grade limit is 15 %, so it zig-zags |
| `dirt` | 4 m | 22 % | 34 % | Elderwood loop, Rustwild camps, the ford track, farm tracks, hill viewpoints |

Highways, lanes and streets are **asphalt** (surface 11), yards / plazas / the runway, taxiway, apron and launch pad
**concrete** (12) — both county-only SURFACES with the road's grip, sink and drag, so they drive exactly like `road`;
the classic map never paints either, and its roads still draw with the `road` layer (`tests/county.test.js` checks).

Gravel and dirt roads **meander** (`meander()`): after smoothing, each point is pushed across the road by a
displacement field (low-frequency noise, a bend every ~90 m, up to 7 m on mountain roads, 5 m on dirt), faded out at
both ends and wherever the road already turns hard. It is ONE field for the whole county, not a wander per road: two
roads routed onto the same grid cells get the same push and stay together (a per-road wander pulled shared tracks
apart and carved 1 m steps between them). `snapToBuilt()` then pulls a later rough road onto an earlier one wherever
they run within 9 m, so where they part they part smoothly.

Router additions (`roads.js`, opt-in, classic unchanged): `heur` (heuristic weight — 1.1 makes county routes fast),
`box` (stay inside the ends' bounding box + m, so a failed search costs milliseconds), `reuse` per call (dirt uses 0.8 so
tracks do not run side by side), and `profile({ cones: true })` (every sample stays within the clamp's reach of both
pins, so a pinned end is never dragged off its height). `unloop()` in countygen.js cuts knots out of a routed path (a
path crossing itself carved a cliff across the road).

The **switchback** climbs a **spur**, not the cliff (`C.switchback`, `spurS` + `traceSwitchback()`):

1. *The spur*: a ramp of ground that runs out of the plateau's south rim down to the vale — its crest falls at 35 %
   (`gA`) and wanders sideways (`wobble`), its core is ~125 m either side of the crest (the width varies down its
   length) and 10 m lower at the edges, then the flanks steepen to ~40 degrees. Past the rim its shoulders round off
   along a wavy line, so it grows out of the cliff. Land rises to it (plus 3 m of noise) wherever it is higher.
2. *The road* is surveyed onto it: a walker steps 2 m at a time across the slope at the angle that makes the ground
   rise at the road's grade (sin a = 0.10 / slope), nudged gently by how far the road has drifted from the ground
   (never more than gently downhill), turning no tighter than a 45 m radius — so each leg curves with the land and
   runs diagonally across the face. Near the flank (a different distance for every leg, 62-118 m from the crest) it
   turns uphill round a hairpin (R 14-18 m, 5.5 % grade) that stops turning when it lines up with the next leg. Once
   the road can reach the top by the crest at the rim it heads there, then runs level onto the plateau.
   Seed 7: 7 legs, 6 hairpins, ~1.6 km, 141 m of climb at an average 9.1 %.
3. *Earthworks*: within 46 m of the road the ground may be no higher than a 1.05 cut bank and no lower than a 0.72
   fill bank reaching out from the road's edge (+0.6 m), so the cuts and fills are planar banks like a real road's,
   painted raw earth / gravel / rock (paint 5). Each hairpin's bowl is level and paved 4 m wider on its inside
   (paint 6), so a long vehicle can swing round.
4. *Guard posts*: `guard_post` objects (white, red band, r 0.12 m, break at 7000 N s) every ~4 m round the outside
   of every hairpin.

`world.switchback = { pts, legs, hairpins: [{ x, z, r, y }], grade }`.
**Bridges** (straight north-south decks, `bridge_deck` / `bridge_rail` / `bridge_pier`): Lindell Crossing (low),
Tollen Gorge Bridge (on the rims, ~50 m over the water, 3 tall piers), Eastwater Bridge (low).

### Sites — the contract later milestones read (`world.sites`)

```js
sites.home      { x, z, y, r, city: 'marrow_flats', place: 'marrow_flats_garage' }      // spawn: Marrow Flats garage yard
sites.flags     []                                                                       // no Flag Run on this map
sites.pads      [{ x, z, y, yaw, vehicle, area, prop? }]   // garages first (4 each: marrow_flats, port_lindell, highgate,
                //  copperton), then depots (2 each), airplane + helicopter (area 'airfield'), 2 harvesters ('farm'),
                //  then prop pads (crates at each depot). The room numbers entities in pad order.
sites.cities    [{ id, name, x, z, y, hx, hz, gates: { n|s|e|w: { x, z, node } } }]   // ids: marrow_flats, port_lindell,
                //  highgate, copperton. y = the town's flat height; hx/hz = half extent to just past the outer street.
sites.places    [{ id, kind, city, name, x, z, y, yaw, r, building, yard?: {x0,z0,x1,z1}, door?: {x,z}, pads?: [pad idx] }]
                // id = '<city>_<kind>'. x,z = where you drive to (the middle of a yard, or the kerb in front of a shop);
                // yaw faces the street (0 = south). building = the object id. kinds and where:
                //   garage x4 (pads), depot x4 (pads), outfitter x4, supply x4, tow_yard (marrow_flats, port_lindell,
                //   copperton), hospital (port_lindell, highgate), fire_station (marrow_flats, port_lindell),
                //   market (marrow_flats), survey_office (highgate), jump_point (Wayfare Field, city null)
sites.shops     [{ id, kind: 'dealer'|'outfitter'|'supply'|'market', place, city, name, x, z, y, yaw, r }]
sites.farms     { town, plots: [{ id, x, z, w, h, yaw: 0, y }]  (10, flat, farm soil),
                  barn: { x, z, y, building, hayBarn }, yard: { x, z, hx, hz, y }, market: 'marrow_flats_market',
                  pads: [harvester pad idx], bales: [object ids] }
sites.fireRisk  [{ id, kind: 'barn'|'hay'|'house'|'crop'|'grass', x, z, y, r, obj?|objs?|plot?, town? }]
sites.rustwild  { name, poly: [[x,z]...], gate: {x,z}, camps: [{ id, name, x, z, y, r, buildings: [ids] }] }   // 5 camps
sites.airport   { name, y, runway, taxiway: {x0,z0,x1,z1,w,y}, apron: {x0,z0,x1,z1,y}, hangars: [{x,z,building}],
                  tower, pads: [plane, heli], jumpPoint: { x, z, y, yaw, r, building } }
sites.runway    { x0, z0, x1, z1, w, y }                // = airport.runway: 1100 x 30 m, east-west, flat to +-0.35 m
sites.launch    { name, x, z, y, r, pad: { x, z, r }, tower, control, road }   // Skyreach: paved disc, > 700 m from towns
sites.survey    [{ id, name, kind: 'summit'|'rim'|'basin'|'mesa', x, z, y }]   // Greyspine Lookout (road to it),
                //  Thornhorn + Wardenspire (the named peaks, ids thornhorn / wardenspire), Copper Knoll, Highgate Rim,
                //  Gorge Overlook, Vale Basin, Redstep Mesa
sites.bridges   [{ x0, z0, x1, z1, w, y, id, name, high }]
sites.ramps     [{ x, z, yaw, len, h, id }]            // six kickers on the dirt tracks
sites.labels    [{ x, z, text, kind: 'city'|'region'|'water'|'crossing'|'place'|'shop'|'base'|'camp'|'view' }]
```

World fields added: `map: 'county'`, `name`, `plateau`, `gorge`, `switchback { pts, legs, hairpins, grade }`; `roads[]` carry
`town` for streets; `roadGraph.nodes[]` carry `town` for gates. Survey kits (M10) may use anywhere the rules allow —
the viewpoints are only named spots.

### Objects (seed 7: ~11.8k collidable, ~29k decor)

* `guard_post` — white posts round the switchback's hairpins (~50 on seed 7), drawn in things.js (look
  `guard_post`), breakable.
* `building` — `{ shape: box (the walls, to the eaves), role, roof: 'flat'|'gable', colour, roofColour, floors,
  windows, town }`, unbreakable. ~240: town lots (`house`, `shop`, `block`), landmarks (role = the place kind),
  `barn`, `hay_barn`, `hangar`, `control_tower`, `jump_point`, `launch_tower`, `launch_control`, `raider_shack`.
  Physics: a plain box collider (no physics change was needed).
* `tree_giant` — 40-60 m tall, trunk 2.8-4.1 m across (r = h / 29), unbreakable; ~55 in the Elderwood, drawn as the
  kit's spruce / fir / pine at full size scaled up whole.
* giant fallen logs — `log` with `giant: true`, r 1.1-1.45 m, 26-40 m long, half buried in an earth berm that comes up
  to ~0.35 m under the top so a car can climb over.
* Scatter uses `COUNTY_SCATTER` through new opt-in `scatterObjects` options (`rules`, `decorRules`, `density`, `step`,
  `decorStep`; a rule may carry `space`, `maxSlope`, `tint`).

### The view

* `world-view/buildings.js` — every building merged into one mesh per 256 m cell (seed 7: 242 buildings in 23
  meshes, 3.9k triangles for all of them), windows painted by the wall shader from metre coordinates, gable / flat roofs; it needs
  its own `defines` (enhance() keys programs by option flags only — without it three reused the rock program and the
  walls came out black).
* `things.js` — `tree_giant` has its own draw distances (`giant`: 1.5x the tree ones); `building` is skipped.
* `ground.js` — two more texture layers, `asphalt` (the kit's gravel, greyed and flattened) and `concrete` (the kit's
  sand, light grey, saw-cut joints every 4 m); a 4th weight attribute `aW3` carries them. The classic map's layers and
  weights are unchanged (its weight for both is always 0).
* `markings.js` — road paint, county only: highways a dashed yellow centre line + white edge lines, lanes a dashed
  white centre line, the switchback a double yellow line; the runway's edge lines, 30 m centre dashes, threshold bars
  and touchdown blocks; the taxiway's yellow line; a yellow ring and cross on the launch pad. Lines stop short of
  junctions and skip bridges. Thin quads 3.5 cm over the ground, one merged mesh per 128 m cell, shown only while
  that cell's ground is at its finest level (coarser ground can sit above or below the true heights).
  `view.debug().markings`.
* `ground.js` — the weight blur keeps three rows of scratch instead of a whole-map float array (113 MB for the county).
* `mapimage.js` — highways in yellow, streets, lanes, mountain gravel, dirt dashed; building footprints.
* `simple-view.js` — buildings are boxes in their own colour.
* `world.html?map=county&at=<place>` — places: home, marrow_flats, port_lindell, street, highway, highgate, copperton,
  switchback, hairpin, peaks, gorge, giants, runway, launch, rustwild, summit, scarp, lake, farm. `&worker=0` builds
  the world on the page. `&view=simple` draws with the plain view.
* Draw calls (seed 7, measured 2026-11-09, shadow passes included): **medium** 1280x720: 96-195 (giant wood 195 /
  1.1 M triangles, towns ~160 / 0.6 M, switchback 156, gorge 178); **low** 402x780: 40-54 calls, 87-188 k triangles.
* Spec: `tests/county.spec.js` (shots `tests/shots/county-*.png`, ~7 min under software rendering). Node:
  `tests/county.test.js` (~25 s).

## The Moon (map `'moon'`, Expansion 1 — groundwork for M12)

`generateWorld({ seed, map: 'moon' })` — code in `moon/`: `moongen.js` (the generator) and `moon-data.js` (every place,
name and number). Same contract and purity rules as the other maps. **2048 m square, 2 m cell, dim 1025** (1.05 M
samples). Generation ~0.85 s in Node 22 on this VM (land ~580 ms — the gradient noise of the highlands — craters 60,
rille 30, surfaces 70, objects 90); in the page it is built in the worker like the county.

```
 z = -1024 north      Farside Depot (supply runs end here)          Lumen Ridge (crest ~158 m, NE)
                      Orrin Crater (huge, NW)  Tumblestone Reach    Scatterstone Field
            ~~~~~~~~~~ Silverthread Rille: ~1.5 km winding channel across the Hush Sea ~~~~~~~~~~
                      Hush Sea (smooth dark plain: speed)                      Kestle Crater (huge, E)
                      Vandry Crater (huge, SW)
 z = +1024 south      Greywatch Base (domes, garage pad, sample drop) · Greywatch Landing (the pad) · Hopper Ramps
```

* **Land**: the **Hush Sea** (an ellipse, its edge wandered by noise) is flat (±1.2 m) and dark; everywhere else is
  the bright rolling **highlands** (16-54 m, the county's gradient noise `gfbm`); the **Lumen Ridge** is a ridged band
  along a line, up to ~120 m above them. A 0.34 m fine undulation everywhere so nothing is billiard-table flat.
* **Craters** (`world.craters` = big + medium; small / tiny only counted in `stats.craters`), each ADDED to the land:
  inside `-D + (D + H) * u^p` (u from the flat floor fraction `f0` to the rim), a raised rim `H`, ejecta
  `H * (1 - t)^2` out to 1.9 R. Three named **giants** (Orrin R ~185, Kestle ~140, Vandry ~120; flat floor, central
  peak, wall ~38 deg) each with a **breach**: within ~25 deg of the bearing to the lowest land round it the wall is a
  straight ramp (~20 deg) and the rim 60 % lower — the drivable way in (`breach: { x, z }`; nothing else is placed in
  its corridor). ~16 **medium** (R 24-62, every third one steep, `p = 3`, ~45 deg walls: they want a run-up; never on a
  slope or a crest), ~190 **small** (R 4-15), ~1400 **tiny** (R 1.6-4). None on the base, the pad, the depot or the rille.
* **The rille** (`world.rille = { pts: [[x, z, floorY]] every 8 m, floorHalf 16, wall 20, depth 9.5, length }`): a
  Chaikin-smoothed control line with a sideways wiggle, carved AFTER the craters: floor = the land along it smoothed
  over ~200 m less the depth (eased to 0 over 150 m at both ends, then held to <= 10 % along), walls a straight 25 deg
  bank rounded into the floor. A 32 m wide floor to drive along; rocks mostly kept off it.
* **Surfaces** (appended to `SURFACES`): `regolith` (13: grip 0.78, sink 0.04, drag 1.25, deep ruts) everywhere,
  `moonrock` (14) where the ground is steeper than ~33 deg, `concrete` on the pads. **Biomes** (appended): `m_mare`,
  `m_highland`, `m_crater`, `m_rille`, `m_base`. No water, no roads (`roads: []`, `roadDist` 999 everywhere).
* **Objects** (~1.9k): rocks (`rock_s/m/l`, `boulder`, grey `tint`, kit looks boulder / slab / shard / stone / rock
  cluster) on a 6 m jittered grid — dense in two named **boulder fields** and the ejecta rings, sparse elsewhere; base
  buildings (`building` boxes with `role`: hab_dome, command, lab_dome, tunnel, garage, sample_drop, solar, mast, depot,
  tank, pad_light); **jump ramps** (wedges: two practice "Hopper Ramps" north of the base, four on the outer aprons of
  medium craters aimed at the bowl). ~12k pebbles in `decor`.

### Moon sites (`world.sites`) — what M11 / M12 read

```js
gravity: 1.62, sky: 'black', space: { hour, sunDir: [x,y,z], planet: { dir, size, name, colour } }   // world fields
sites.home       { x, z, y, r, place: 'greywatch_garage' }       // spawn by the rover garage
sites.pads       [{ x, z, y, yaw, vehicle: 'moon_rover' (or opts.vehicles cycled), area }]  // 4 at the garage, 2 at the
                 //  depot, then prop pads (a crate at the sample drop and at the depot)
sites.base       { id: 'greywatch', name, x, z, y, r, buildings: [object ids] }
sites.garage     { x, z, y, building, pads: [pad idx] }           sites.sampleDrop { id, name, x, z, y, r, building }
sites.landing    { id, name, x, z, y, r, pad: { x, z, r }, lights }   // where the landing pod / rocket comes down
sites.depot      { id, name, x, z, y, r, building, buildings, pads }  // Farside Depot, > 1.2 km from the base
sites.places     [{ id, kind: 'garage'|'sample_drop'|'landing_pad'|'depot', ... }]   // county-style places
sites.samples    [{ id, name, kind, x, z, y, r }]   // 7: orrin_floor, rille_bend, lumen_foot, scatterstone, kestle_rim,
                 //  bright_pit (the biggest medium crater well away from the others), vandry_floor — all > 150 m apart
sites.survey     [{ id, name, kind: 'summit'|'rim'|'flat'|'basin', x, z, y }]   // lumen_crest, orrin_rim, hush_flat,
                 //  kestle_basin
sites.ramps      [{ x, z, yaw, len, h, id, ramp, name }]   sites.craters (= world.craters)   sites.fields [{ id, name, x, z, r, rocks }]
world.ridge      { name, line, crest: { x, z, y } }        world.mare { name, x, z, rx, rz }
```

`worldGravity(world)` / `worldSky(world)` (worldgen.js): 9.81 / 'day' for the classic world and the county (they carry
no field, so their hashes did not move), 1.62 / 'black' here. **Physics still uses 9.81** (`js/phys/physics.js`
`new RAPIER.World({ y: -9.81 })` and vehicle.js) — M11 / M12 wire `worldGravity()` in.

### The Moon in the view

* `world-view/index.js`: `world.sky === 'black'` → grass, light shafts and water off; the highdef sky is kept for its
  shadow rig but its dome, clouds, moon and stars are hidden (`applySpace()`): black background, no environment map, fog
  0, the sun from `world.space.sunDir` (3.4, white), hemisphere 0.16 — shadows read nearly black. `setTime` /
  `setWeather` do nothing there. The black-frame safety net only looks at the bottom of the screen on a black world.
* `world-view/space.js` — the backdrop shared by the Moon, the station and the plain view: 2-3k stars (one Points), the
  planet (a lit sphere with a day / night side from the sun, a seeded painted map, an air rim; `planet.tilt` picks the
  face you see) and an additive sun disc. 3-4 draws, a group that follows the camera at 0.9 x its far plane.
* `ground.js` — `buildGroundTextures(size, aniso, 'moon')` greys every layer (regolith uses the sand layer, moonrock
  the rock layer: nothing new painted). The classic / county look is unchanged.
* `mapimage.js` / `simple-view.js` — regolith and moonrock colours; the plain view has the black sky and backdrop.
* `world.html?map=moon&at=<place>` — home, base, landing, depot, orrin, breach, kestle, vandry, rille, ridge, mare,
  boulders, jump, planet, overview.

## Lantern Station (map `'station'`, Expansion 1 — groundwork for M11)

`generateWorld({ map: 'station' })` — code in `station/`: `stationgen.js` and `station-data.js`. An **interior for
zero-g floating**, the same for every seed. It fills the world contract with a tiny flat heightfield (128 m, 4 m cell,
`heightAt` = -60, far below the hull — nothing stands on it) and `world.interior = true`.

```
                     Bunkroom (4 bunks)
                           |
 Docking Port ======== Hub ======== Lab ======== Greenhouse        x east, y up, z south; the planet is BELOW (-y)
 (rocket hatch, W end)     |  \
                       Airlock  Observation Cupola (under the hub, glass floor)
```

* **Rooms** are axis-aligned boxes (`c`, inside half-sizes `h`), **tunnels** 3 m square doors joining two rooms along
  one axis (the generator checks they line up). Walls are 0.3 m thick; each face is one slab, or four round its opening.
* `world.objects` = every panel as `kind: 'hull'`, `shape: box`, base at `o.y` (like every box object), yaw 0, `room`
  (room or tunnel id), `glass: true` for a window (cupola floor + side, lab north wall, greenhouse roof, bunkroom), `hatch:
  true` for a closed hatch (the docking hatch on the dock's west end, the airlock's outer hatch). 130 panels — a physics
  that builds fixed box colliders from objects gets the whole hull, walls to push off included.
* `world.station = { name, rooms, tunnels, doors, handholds (65 rails 0.12 m off the walls: { x, y, z, axis, len, r,
  room }), spots, lights, props, spawn, bounds }`. **Spots**: dock_hatch (spawn: where the rocket docks), hub_centre,
  cupola_window, lab_bench, lab_window, greenhouse_rows, bunk_1..4, airlock_inner, airlock_outer.
  `sites.dock` (the hatch on the west end), `sites.airlock { inner, outer }`, `sites.home` = the spawn.
* Helpers (stationgen.js): `insideStation(world, x, y, z)` -> the room / tunnel id or null; `solidAt(world, x, y, z, pad)`
  -> the panel there or null. The test floats a line from every room's middle to the next one's and checks it never
  comes within 0.4 m of a panel; and that straight out of every room in all six directions you hit a panel.
* `gravity: 0`, `sky: 'black'`, `space.planet` fills the view below (`size` 0.62).

**The view** (`world-view/station.js`): `createWorldView` hands a station world to `createStationView` — the same
contract (update / render / debug / mapImage / setQuality …; tracks, dust, breaking are no-ops). One merged mesh for
the hull (panel lines from a canvas texture laid in metres, floor / wall / ceiling tinted by which way the face points,
each room its own tint), one each for hatches (hazard stripes), glass, light strips and props, one instanced mesh for
the handholds, a point light per room (none on `low`: a brighter hemisphere instead), the space backdrop through the
windows. ~10 draw calls, ~11k triangles. `drawStationMap()` is the top-down plan for the map / HUD; the plain view
(`simple-view.js`) draws the same meshes without point lights.
`world.html?map=station&at=` dock, hub, cupola, lab, greenhouse, sleep, airlock, outside.

Tests: `node --test prototypes/roverlands/tests/moon.test.js` (`MOON_SEED=1234` for another seed) and
`flock /home/radgh/claude/agent/roverlands-pw.lock npx playwright test prototypes/roverlands/tests/moon.spec.js`
(shots `tests/shots/moon-*.png`, `station-*.png`).
